hints: Choose two rows; a rectangle needs two columns black in both rows.
If c columns are black in both rows, they form c*(c-1)/2 rectangles.
Pack each row into machine-word bitsets and count bits in pairwise ANDs.
analogy: Each shared black column is a possible side; choose any two sides for a rectangle.
example: Two rows 1101 and 1110 share black columns 1 and 2, producing one rectangle.
algorithm: Represent each row as a bitset. For every pair of rows, AND their bitsets and count the set bits c, then add c*(c-1)/2 to the answer. Use a wide integer for the total.
correctness: Every valid rectangle has a unique pair of rows and a unique pair of columns black in both. The binomial count enumerates exactly those column pairs for each row pair.
complexity: For n rows and machine word size w, O(n^3/w+n^2) word operations and O(n^2/w) words of space.
